data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Coupled oscillators in physics follow deterministic dynamics, whereas service operators may use stochastic or varied thresholds.","Biological flocks may avoid synchrony through local interactions, while network services synchronize through global market signals."],"overturn_conditions":["Operators introduce jitter or randomization in their monitoring and response thresholds, breaking the synchronization.","The external signal is not strong enough to entrain the operators' behavior."],"shared_structure":["Independent oscillators (services) driven by a common external periodic force (market signal/metric) will synchronize.","Synchronization leads to correlated phase transitions (failures) across the population."],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_002"],"transfer_claims":["If a decentralized network's independent operators synchronize on external signals, it will exhibit correlated failures despite decentralization.","A large service with diverse internal policies may avoid such synchronization, making it more resilient."]},"claim":"A decentralized network is NOT more resilient because if all small operators monitor the same metrics for uptime and independently decide to reboot or scale based on the same threshold, they will oscillate in phase, creating a self-organized criticality where the network appears independent but fails in perfect synchrony.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Operators use randomized or jittered thresholds for scaling and rebooting.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service also monitors the same metrics and is susceptible to the same oscillations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized services often rely on similar monitoring signals. If independent operators independently optimize for the same metrics using similar thresholds, their responses to external load can synchronize. This creates self-organized criticality where the system appears independent but fails in perfect synchrony due to the shared external signal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
